partner_result_applied.application: Used finite-mixture approximation plus Jensen and Fatou to prove exact same-extreme L^p Fourier localization for every p>=1, including iid Fejer L2 collision energy.

new_mathematics.statement: For every measurable P, nonnegative Borel w and p>=1, the supremum of integral w(t)|E exp(itP)|^p dt over all cap-one product laws equals the supremum over compact finite-fragment unit-set product indicators. The p=2 Fejer energy therefore localizes with the same extreme law on both iid copies.

For every beta>0 and p>0, no universal bound exists for integral (1+|t|)^beta |phi_Q(t)|^p dt under the full target hypotheses; failure already occurs for A=I_3 and iid finite-fragment cap-one laws supported in [1,10].

unresolved_implication: Prove the dimension-free unweighted L1 Fourier estimate or direct small-ball bound from only the three-large-eigenvalue hypothesis. Positive polynomial weighted Fourier moments cannot be required uniformly; any such moment must arise from additional branch-specific structure.
next_step: Keep global/same-law finite-fragment localization intact and apply it to an aggregate-before-inversion unweighted Fourier or small-ball mechanism; do not fragmentwise rescale or rely on a universal positive weighted Fourier moment.
